description: A patch cable colour manager, giving new cables colours from a list you choose and offering highlighting for tracing cables around a patch.
notes: new cables take their colour from the checked entries in the colour list, cycling through them in order; Shift and a function key checks or unchecks one of the first 25 colours.
a collection is a saved set of checked colours; Control or Command and a function key switches to one of the first 25 collections.
the checkbox above the colour list checks or unchecks every colour, the plus icon opens the page for making a new colour, and the icon beside it opens the collections page.
the menu icon at the top of the colour list opens Select All Colors, Unselect All Colors, Recolor All Wires..., Add New Color ..., Collections..., Save as Collection and Load collection...
that same menu ends with Settings..., whose page carries Variations, the three highlighting choices, Keep colors on redo and 3D billboard; none of it is on the panel's right-click menu.
right-clicking a colour in the list gives Edit..., Color one wire..., Move Up, Move Down and Delete Color...
with variation switched on, each new cable's colour is randomly varied, and three sliders set how far the hue, the lightness and the saturation may wander.
with highlighting switched on, the cables are faded except those connected to the module the pointer is over.
the control at the top right switches the module to a billboard view for use as a key in a video, and the arrow at the top left switches back.
the module shrinks to 1HP with its Minimize control and comes back with Restore, and the rest of the rack shifts to close and reopen the gap.
the colours stay with the patch after the module is removed, but highlighting stops working without it; the settings themselves are global rather than saved with the patch.
a second wire manager in the same patch only costs CPU, since one of them does the colouring.
menu: Visuals — a submenu of Blue, Dark and Light for the colour scheme, plus Flat for a look without the 3D shading. The choice covers every SubmarineFree module and is kept outside the patch.
